definition: Means–ends analysis (MEA) is a problem solving technique used commonly in artificial intelligence (AI) for limiting search in AI programs.
details: MEA was designed by two scientist Allen Newel and Herbert A. Simon in 1957,[1] lateron, the idea of MEA led to the General Problem Solver, with J.C Shaw.[2] It is also a technique used at least since the 1950s as a creativity tool, most frequently mentioned in engineering books on design methods. MEA is also related to the means–ends chain approach used commonly in consumer behavior analysis. It is also a way to clarify one's thoughts when embarking on a mathematical proof.
